approved: Climate Change (National Framework for Adaptation and Mitigation) (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2020
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would amend several Commonwealth laws to support a new national climate framework.
It would repeal the Climate Change Authority Act 2011 to create an independent Climate Change Commission that advises the government and parliament.
The bill would require Commonwealth entities to consider and report on climate change risks under the Public Governance Performance and Accountability Act 2013.

Commonwealth entities and their accountable authorities.

The member for Mayo seconded the Climate Change (National Framework for Adaptation and Mitigation) (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2020, calling for a free parliamentary vote and urging action to provide business certainty. The speech cited the United Kingdom’s 12-year framework and New Zealand’s legislation, and warned of catastrophic impacts for regional Australia and Pacific islands without action.

The speaker moved the second reading of a bill to establish an independent Climate Change Commission, replacing the Climate Change Authority, with membership selected by a bipartisan committee and including an Indigenous commissioner. The bill also mandates that Commonwealth entities consider and disclose climate risks, aligning public sector requirements with private sector standards.

The seconder supported the bill, arguing it would help regional Australia both protect at-risk industries—like dairy, wine, alpine tourism and the Mansfield/Bright tourism economy—and seize clean energy opportunities such as zero-carbon hydrogen and steel. The speech cited CSIRO projections of up to 36% rainfall decline in north-east Victoria, a 1°C temperature increase already observed, and a 44% increase in extreme fire danger days under runaway climate change.
